transcript:
Fireflies.ai meeting transcript

Title: Demo: Console Usage Insights (routes + CSV export) - BrightLoop
Date: 2026-02-19
Time: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 43 min

Attendees
Redwood Inference: Markus Klein, Felix Schneider, Paula Mendes
BrightLoop: Jenna Park, Miguel Santos, Priya Nair, Samir Qureshi

Summary (auto-generated)
- Redwood demoed the new Console Usage Insights experience focused on cost drivers by route and model.
- BrightLoop asked how to filter by environment/region and how route naming works (SDK vs gateway).
- Deep questions on CSV export limits, schema stability, and audit logging for exports.
- Priya (FinOps) raised concerns about reconciling route-level costs with invoices; Redwood explained common sources of mismatch (time windows, late data, discounts/commitments, rounding).

Topics (auto-generated)
1) Route dimension + naming conventions
2) Cost drivers table + filters
3) Route detail view (model breakdown + week-over-week deltas)
4) Export flow (CSV + JSON) and limits
5) Invoice reconciliation + known gaps
6) Security/RBAC + audit logs

Questions (captured)
- Can we filter spend by environment (prod vs staging) and region?
- If a request falls back to a different model, does the cost stay attributed to the original route?
- What’s the max time range / rows for CSV export?
- How stable is the export schema over time (will columns change)?
- Why does console cost not match the invoice total to the dollar?
- Are exports audit-logged and can we show that in a compliance review?

Transcript

[00:00] Markus Klein: Cool. Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I’m Markus. I work with the go-to-market team at Redwood. Felix is here from console engineering, and Paula is the PM for the usage insights project.

[00:12] Jenna Park: Hey. Jenna, platform. We’ve got Miguel from backend, Priya from finance slash FinOps, and Samir from security.

[00:21] Markus Klein: Perfect. Goal today is show the in-console usage insights—cost drivers by route and by model—and then focus on the CSV export, since that came up in the last email.

[00:33] Priya Nair: Yes please. I’m mostly here for the export and reconciliation story.

[00:38] Markus Klein: Great. Felix, do you want to drive the screen?

[00:41] Felix Schneider: Yep. Sharing now.

[00:48] Felix Schneider: Okay, so you’re in Redwood Console, left nav “Usage Insights.” This is behind a feature flag for most orgs right now. The main view is “Routes.” It ranks by total cost over the selected time window.

[01:04] Miguel Santos: When you say routes, is that like, our HTTP endpoints?

[01:08] Felix Schneider: Exactly. It’s a “route” dimension that you can supply, or we can derive from gateway paths depending on your deployment. Paula can clarify the canonical definition, but practically, you tag requests with something like `route=/v1/chat` or `route=chat.create`.

[01:23] Paula Mendes: Yeah. Think of it as a stable identifier for a developer-defined endpoint or feature. We really want to avoid including user IDs or tenant IDs in it.

[01:33] Samir Qureshi: So it’s a custom header or param?

[01:36] Felix Schneider: In the SDKs it’s an option, and in gateway setups it can be mapped from request metadata. Under the hood it becomes a telemetry field, so we enforce normalization rules.

[01:48] Felix Schneider: On the right, you’ve got filters: time range, environment, region, project, deployment mode. Here I’m filtering to “prod”, region “us-east”, last 7 days.

[02:03] Jenna Park: We have prod and staging as separate projects today.

[02:06] Felix Schneider: Then it’ll be straightforward—you can filter by project. If you also send an explicit environment tag, it’ll show up there too, but project separation is usually enough.

[02:16] Priya Nair: The table shows “cost” and “unit cost.” What’s unit cost in this context?

[02:22] Felix Schneider: Unit cost is effectively cost per 1K tokens, normalized for the selected window. We show total, input tokens, output tokens, cached tokens (if applicable), and a GPU time proxy for some deployments.

[02:37] Miguel Santos: Cached tokens meaning prefix cache?

[02:40] Felix Schneider: Yeah, prefix/KV caching. It’s not always 1:1 with billing because billing can have different treatments, but it’s a very useful driver signal.

[02:51] Priya Nair: Not always 1:1 is where I start sweating.

[02:54] Markus Klein: We’ll get to that, I promise.

[02:57] Felix Schneider: You can click a route. Let’s click “chat.completions” here. Route detail view shows a time series, p50/p95 latency, error rates, and then a model breakdown.

[03:12] Felix Schneider: So for this route, 68% spend is “rw-llama-70b” and 24% is “rw-llama-70b-quant” and there’s a small tail where fallback hit “rw-mixtral.”

[03:26] Miguel Santos: Wait, fallback is captured here?

[03:29] Felix Schneider: Yup. That was one of our core requirements. Cost stays attributed to the original route, and we break down by actual model served. So you can see when routing policy is changing your spend.

[03:42] Jenna Park: That’s actually great. We’ve been blind when the system switches models.

[03:47] Felix Schneider: Exactly. And then “What changed” is this delta widget: compares selected window vs previous window. Like, “+18% cost week-over-week,” and it’ll highlight whether it’s from token volume or unit cost shifts.

[04:03] Priya Nair: Does it tell you why unit cost changed? Like price changes?

[04:07] Paula Mendes: It won’t diagnose “pricing changed” as a narrative in GA. It’s more “input tokens up, output tokens up, cache hit rate down, model mix changed.” Pricing changes are rare; usually it’s model mix or prompt length drift.

[04:21] Samir Qureshi: On RBAC: if I’m scoped to a project, can I still see org-wide route spend?

[04:26] Felix Schneider: No. It respects org/project boundaries. If your role only has access to project A, you can’t query project B. That includes exports.

[04:37] Samir Qureshi: Good.

[04:39] Felix Schneider: Okay, export. Top right: “Export report.” When you click it, you pick CSV or JSON. It creates an export job with the filters and time window baked in.

[04:52] Priya Nair: Does the export include the filters used?

[04:55] Felix Schneider: Yes. The export metadata includes time range, timezone, project, region, deployment mode, route filter if applied.

[05:03] Priya Nair: Wait, timezone? Which timezone is default?

[05:06] Felix Schneider: UI shows in your org setting timezone, but the export includes a UTC timestamp column and the window boundaries. We try to make it explicit because reconciliation issues often come from “I thought it was local time.”

[05:20] Priya Nair: Thank you.

[05:22] Miguel Santos: What’s the grain of the export? Per route? Per hour?

[05:26] Felix Schneider: You can export aggregated rows: route x model for the selected window, and optionally a time-bucketed export (hourly or daily) depending on the range. For big ranges, we push people to daily to keep row counts sane.

[05:42] Priya Nair: “Keep row counts sane” meaning there’s a limit.

[05:46] Felix Schneider: Yes. There are limits. We cap the max time range and max rows. If you ask for, say, 90 days hourly across all routes, it’ll either fail fast or ask you to narrow filters.

[05:58] Markus Klein: The rough intent is: export is designed for finance ops workflows, but bounded so it doesn’t take down the analytics cluster.

[06:06] Priya Nair: What are the actual caps? We need to plan automation.

[06:11] Felix Schneider: In the current beta, CSV export is capped at 200k rows and about 250MB uncompressed, and there’s also a runtime timeout on the job. If you hit it, we recommend narrowing or using daily bucket. These numbers might shift slightly before GA.

[06:31] Priya Nair: Okay. And schema stability? I don’t want columns changing under us.

[06:36] Paula Mendes: We’re versioning the export schema. There’s a schema version field. If we add columns, we do it in a backwards compatible way. If we ever had to rename/remove, it would be a version bump and we’d provide a heads-up window.

[06:54] Priya Nair: So like, v1, v2.

[06:56] Paula Mendes: Exactly.

[07:00] Samir Qureshi: Audit logs for the export. We need: who exported, when, what scope.

[07:07] Felix Schneider: Yep. Export create and export download both generate audit events. It captures actor, org, project, report type, filters, time range, and the resulting file size.

[07:20] Samir Qureshi: Is the “filters” field too verbose? Like does it include route names?

[07:26] Felix Schneider: It includes route filter value if you exported a single route, yes. If that’s sensitive, it’s something we can discuss. But most customers want the evidence.

[07:36] Jenna Park: Route names aren’t sensitive for us.

[07:38] Priya Nair: It’s fine.

[07:40] Markus Klein: Priya, do you want to jump into invoice reconciliation now?

[07:44] Priya Nair: Yeah. So in the past with other providers, dashboards never match invoices. I need to be able to explain differences. Like our CFO wants to tie spend to feature, but the invoice is the source of truth.

[07:59] Paula Mendes: Totally. We’re being pretty explicit in docs that “Usage Insights” is an operational attribution view, and “Billing” is the legal invoice view. They should be close, but there are known deltas.

[08:10] Priya Nair: What deltas.

[08:12] Paula Mendes: The most common ones:
- Time window boundaries and timezone differences.
- Late-arriving metering events: some token counts finalize slightly after the request completes.
- Rounding at different aggregation levels.
- Credits, discounts, or committed spend constructs that appear on the invoice but not in route attribution.
- Cross-project or shared charges if you’re on Dedicated capacity (depending how it’s contracted).

[08:35] Miguel Santos: Late arriving? Like how late.

[08:38] Paula Mendes: Usually minutes, occasionally longer if there’s a retry or an upstream queue. Our SLO target is near-real-time, but “near” is doing some work. That’s why we also show “data freshness” in the UI.

[08:52] Felix Schneider: Here—top right you see “Data updated 6 minutes ago.” If there’s lag, we display it and our internal alarms fire.

[09:02] Priya Nair: Okay but invoice is monthly. Do you have a monthly export that matches invoice?

[09:07] Markus Klein: Today, exports are bounded by retention and job limits. You can do 30 days daily pretty comfortably. If you need exact invoice-grade reconciliation, we can also provide billing exports via the billing system, but that’s different.

[09:21] Priya Nair: So I might need both. One for chargeback by route, another for invoice.

[09:26] Paula Mendes: That’s the typical pattern.

[09:28] Priya Nair: What about cached tokens? Do they reduce cost in the dashboard? Because invoice might treat it differently.

[09:35] Paula Mendes: We break out cached tokens separately and the cost field already reflects your effective cost as metered by our serving layer, but invoice may include other line items, like minimums or support, and rounding. Also, some customers have pricing where cache hits are priced differently; it depends on your contract.

[09:56] Jenna Park: We’re on hosted API now. No dedicated commits yet.

[10:00] Markus Klein: Right.

[10:02] Priya Nair: So for hosted, will the sum of route costs equal the invoice usage line?

[10:07] Paula Mendes: It should be close if you align time windows in UTC and exclude credits/adjustments, but we don’t promise exact cents-level match. There can be small timing and rounding differences.

[10:18] Priya Nair: That’s… honest. I prefer honest.

[10:21] Felix Schneider: Also, you’ll see “Unknown route” if requests aren’t tagged. That can make the route breakdown look like it’s missing spend when actually it’s just un-attributed.

[10:32] Miguel Santos: Yeah that’s on us.

[10:33] Jenna Park: We have a gateway. We can inject it there.

[10:36] Paula Mendes: Great. We also enforce cardinality guardrails. If your gateway tags with raw paths like `/v1/users/1234/chat`, that will explode. We want templated routes like `/v1/users/:id/chat` or a logical name.

[10:53] Miguel Santos: Is there a hard limit on route name length?

[10:56] Felix Schneider: Yes. We truncate and normalize. There’s also allowed characters. If it violates rules, it may be hashed or mapped to “other/invalid.” The goal is the system stays stable.

[11:10] Miguel Santos: Okay. We’ll do logical names.

[11:13] Samir Qureshi: Export security: can a user export and then share the link externally?

[11:18] Felix Schneider: Download is authenticated. Links expire. And access is checked again at download time.

[11:25] Samir Qureshi: Good. Retention of exports?

[11:28] Felix Schneider: Export artifacts are retained for a short period; the audit event remains longer per audit retention policy. We can share exact defaults after the call.

[11:40] Priya Nair: Another reconciliation question: does the cost in usage insights include retries? Like if the request failed and retried.

[11:47] Paula Mendes: If tokens were generated and metered, that counts. We also show error rate so you can correlate “spend went up because errors and retries.” But we don’t do full anomaly detection in this first release.

[12:02] Jenna Park: Can you filter by erroring routes? Like show routes with highest error rate.

[12:07] Felix Schneider: Not yet as a sort key, but you can view error rate columns and we’re considering additional sort options. Today it’s primarily cost-ranked.

[12:18] Markus Klein: We can capture that as feedback.

[12:20] Felix Schneider: One more thing—route detail includes model breakdown plus latency by model. So if fallback to a smaller model improves latency but changes cost, you can see it.

[12:33] Miguel Santos: That’s helpful for our SLOs.

[12:35] Priya Nair: If we export, can we get both cost and latency fields?

[12:39] Felix Schneider: Yes. You can include performance metrics columns—p50, p95, error rate—depending on export type. The “finance” export is cost-focused; the “ops” export includes perf.

[12:55] Priya Nair: Great. As long as cost columns are stable.

[13:00] Paula Mendes: Cost columns we expect to keep stable. If we add fields like “gpu_time_ms,” we’ll add them as additional columns.

[13:10] Markus Klein: Can we talk implementation for a second? Miguel, you asked earlier about tagging.

[13:15] Miguel Santos: Yeah. We use your TypeScript SDK in one service and direct REST in another. Can both send route?

[13:22] Felix Schneider: Yes. TS SDK will have a `route` option on the request helper, and for REST you can send a standard header. We’ll send you the exact header name.

[13:34] Miguel Santos: If we forget to set it, it becomes unknown.

[13:37] Felix Schneider: Exactly.

[13:40] Jenna Park: How does it interact with multi-tenant? We might want route by tenant later.

[13:45] Paula Mendes: That’s currently out of scope. We’re not allowing arbitrary custom dimensions beyond route/model right now. For chargeback by tenant, the recommendation is to use projects or org structure, or do post-processing outside Redwood.

[14:02] Priya Nair: That’s not ideal but okay.

[14:05] Markus Klein: Many customers start with route chargeback and then decide if they need tenant-level chargeback.

[14:12] Samir Qureshi: Any concerns with PII in exports?

[14:16] Felix Schneider: Exports are aggregates, not per-request payloads. No prompts, no completions. Just metrics.

[14:22] Samir Qureshi: Perfect.

[14:24] Markus Klein: I want to be respectful of time. Maybe we do quick recap and next steps.

[14:30] Priya Nair: Before that, can I ask one more: If I export “last month” and then later re-export, will numbers change due to late data?

[14:38] Paula Mendes: Good question. Very recent windows can shift slightly as late metering arrives. Older windows should be stable. We’re also exploring “finalized” markers, but not in the first GA.

[14:52] Priya Nair: Okay, so for monthly close we should pull after a buffer.

[14:55] Paula Mendes: Exactly—many teams do T+1 or T+2 days.

[15:01] Markus Klein: Cool. Recap: Felix showed routes ranked by cost, filters, route detail with model breakdown and deltas, and export job flow. Next steps: we’ll enable the beta in your staging org, send schema docs and a sample export, and Miguel will add route tags for your key endpoints. Then we’ll reconvene to review data and talk reconciliation.

[15:23] Jenna Park: Sounds good.

[15:25] Miguel Santos: Yep.

[15:26] Priya Nair: Works.

[15:28] Samir Qureshi: Please include the audit log event names in the follow-up.

[15:32] Felix Schneider: Will do.

[15:35] Markus Klein: Great. Thanks everyone.

(Transcript continues with Q&A and scheduling; some portions omitted by recorder due to crosstalk.)

[17:10] Jenna Park: Sorry one last operational question—can we pin filters in the URL? For sharing internally.

[17:17] Felix Schneider: Yes, the page state is reflected in the URL query params. Exports are separate though.

[18:02] Priya Nair: And export is async job, right.

[18:04] Felix Schneider: Correct.

[21:45] Miguel Santos: If we do a model migration, can we see before/after by route.

[21:49] Felix Schneider: Yes. That’s basically what the “what changed” view is for.

[26:30] Samir Qureshi: Do you support SSO for who can export.

[26:34] Markus Klein: Yes. RBAC and SSO/SAML are supported for enterprise tiers. Export permission can be controlled by role.

[31:12] Priya Nair: Okay. So action items are: you send us schema and we send you our desired weekly report.

[31:18] Markus Klein: Exactly.

[42:20] Markus Klein: Alright, I’ll drop. Thanks again.
